heading: What to wear to a mehndi ceremony

p: Green is the classic mehndi colour across North Indian, Punjabi, Gujarati and Muslim weddings – it echoes the henna leaves and looks fresh in daytime photos. Mint, sage, bottle green, teal and olive all work, and a touch of yellow, pink or gota keeps it festive. Every outfit here is a full set or Anarkali in the green family, chosen from our own Jaipur collection.

list: Sleeves: elbow or three-quarter sleeves keep your hands and wrists free while the henna dries.
Fabric: cotton, chiffon or a light taffeta silk – you will sit for a long time, often outdoors.
Fit: a kurta set or a flared Anarkali lets you sit cross-legged and dance at the sangeet that often follows.
Dupatta: pin it, or keep a light one, so it does not smudge wet henna.

p: Close family often coordinate colours – our group & bridesmaid orders stitch matching outfits to each person's size. Guests can pick any green shade; avoid head-to-toe red, which is usually kept for the bride.

faq: What colour should I wear to a mehndi?
Green is the traditional mehndi colour – mint, sage, bottle green, teal or olive. Yellow and bright florals also work. Avoid head-to-toe bridal red.
What sleeves are best for a mehndi?
Elbow-length or three-quarter sleeves, so the henna on your hands and arms can dry without smudging.
Can I get matching mehndi outfits for the bride's sisters?
Yes. Our group orders stitch matching outfits to each person's measurements and ship them together.
